question: Comparing the unilateral (1 tail) and bilateral hypothesis tests (2 tails):

options.opa: Bilateral tests always give higher p values.
options.opb: Bilateral tests always give lower p values.
options.opc: If a unilateral test is significant, so will the bilateral test.
options.opd: A bilateral test is more sensitive than a unilateral test.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Unilateral hypothesis test -> tests the hypothesis in one direction only -> 90% CHAIN: Bilateral hypothesis test -> tests the hypothesis in both directions -> 90% CHAIN: Bilateral tests always give two p values, one for each direction -> 90% CHAIN: Unilateral tests always give one p value -> 90% CHAIN: If a unilateral test is significant, the bilateral test may or may not be significant -> 70% CHAIN: A bilateral test is more comprehensive as it considers both directions -> 80% CHAIN: Bilateral tests can be more sensitive in detecting effects that go in either direction -> 90%
analysis: In hypothesis testing, the choice between a unilateral and bilateral test depends on the research question and the specific hypothesis being tested. Bilateral tests consider the possibility of effects in both directions, while unilateral tests focus on effects in only one direction. The choice between the two types of tests should be based on the research question and prior knowledge.
